# Generational Wealth

> Generational Wealth is a disciplined swing & scalp trading community — a private Discord room where members get real-time trade callouts with defined entries, targets and invalidation, daily market commentary, and a risk-first system built to keep traders in the game. Membership is $120/month, billed via Patreon, cancel anytime.

Site: https://gwhlds.com
Operated by: Generational Wealth Holdings Corp.

**Important:** Generational Wealth is an educational trading community. It is NOT a registered broker-dealer, investment adviser, or signal-selling service, and it does not manage money or guarantee returns. All content is educational only.

## What Generational Wealth actually is

- A **private Discord community** for day, swing and scalp traders across forex, futures and equities.
- Every callout ships with a **clear entry level, defined upside targets, and a written invalidation point** — so the risk-to-reward is on the table before you enter.
- The room runs one **risk-first system**: position size comes from a fixed risk rule, not conviction. Losses stay small; winners are allowed to run.
- Members range from complete beginners to full-time traders. The education is the product as much as the callouts are.

## The Method — the three principles under every trade

1. **Break & hold.** We never chase. Price has to break clean through the called level *and hold* as the candle closes before anyone enters. Confirmation first, every single time.
2. **Know your next.** Every callout ships with a clear entry level, defined upside targets, and the next level price aims for — a plan before you click buy.
3. **Trail & protect.** As targets print one by one, the stop trails behind them to protect the gain. Profit that is given back was never profit.

## Membership

- **Price:** $120 per month, billed through Patreon.
- **Join:** https://www.patreon.com/Generational_Wealth/join
- **Cancel:** anytime, directly through Patreon.
- **Includes:** private Discord access, real-time callouts with levels, daily commentary and breakdowns, and the risk-first education system.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is Generational Wealth?**
A private, membership-based swing and scalp trading community on Discord. Members receive real-time trade callouts with defined entries, targets and invalidation levels, plus daily market commentary and education built around a risk-first system.

**How much does it cost?**
$120 per month, billed via Patreon. There is no long-term contract and members can cancel at any time.

**Is this financial advice?**
No. Generational Wealth Holdings Corp. is not a registered broker-dealer or investment adviser. Everything published is educational only and is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any instrument. Trading carries substantial risk of loss.

**Do I need experience to join?**
No. The room is built for beginners through advanced traders. New members are taught the same risk-first process the experienced members run, starting with position sizing and invalidation.

**What markets does the room trade?**
Primarily forex and futures, with equities setups as they appear. The method — break and hold, defined targets, trailing protection — is applied the same way across all of them.

**Is it day trading or swing trading?**
Both. It is a swing *and* scalp room. Some setups are intraday scalps; others are held for days. Both are sized from the same risk rule.

**Are results guaranteed?**
No. No trading community can guarantee results, and Generational Wealth does not. Every trade a member takes is their own decision and their own risk.

- [What Is a Liquidity Grab? Stop Hunts Explained](https://gwhlds.com/hub/liquidity-grab-stop-hunt.html): why stop orders cluster just beyond obvious levels, the measured asymmetry in where they sit, why triggering them is an ordinary execution incentive rather than a conspiracy, how to tell a grab from a genuine breakdown after the close, and four defences that do not require predicting one.

- [Why Trading Indicators Lag (And What to Do)](https://gwhlds.com/hub/why-indicators-lag.html): the arithmetic that puts a 20-period average nearly ten bars in the past, why shortening the setting trades lag for false signals rather than removing it, why so-called leading indicators are not leading, why optimising settings on history is a data-snooping trap, and the four uses that survive.

- [Forex Trading Guide: How the Market Works](https://gwhlds.com/hub/forex-trading-guide.html): the pillar guide to foreign exchange — why there is no central exchange, the BIS turnover figures, currency pairs, pip and lot arithmetic, the four sessions and the London–New York overlap, how leverage really changes your risk, what moves currencies, and the three costs that erode an edge.
- [What Is a Pip? How to Calculate Pip Value](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-a-pip.html): the pip as a unit of distance rather than money, why yen pairs use the second decimal place, what a pipette is, the two-line formula for pip value in all three account-currency cases, a pip value table by lot size, and how pip distance feeds position sizing.
- [Forex Sessions Explained: London, NY, Tokyo](https://gwhlds.com/hub/forex-sessions-explained.html): the four sessions with hours in UTC and Eastern Time, BIS data on where FX trading actually takes place, why the London–New York overlap carries the tightest spreads and largest ranges, how daylight saving shifts every session table, and how to choose a session around a job.
- [Best Forex Pairs for Beginners](https://gwhlds.com/hub/best-forex-pairs-for-beginners.html): the four criteria that make a pair beginner-friendly, dollar pairs ranked by BIS April 2025 spot turnover, a pair-by-pair shortlist, why exotics and high-range crosses cost more than they appear to, and why one pair traded properly beats five watched badly.
- [What Is the Spread in Forex?](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-the-spread-in-forex.html): the bid-ask gap you pay on every trade, how it is quoted in pips, and what it costs over a year.
- [What Is Swap in Forex?](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-swap-in-forex.html): overnight financing and rollover explained — the interest rate differential, triple-swap Wednesday, and swap-free accounts.
- [How News Events Move Forex Pairs](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-news-moves-forex-pairs.html): why price trades the surprise not the number, what happens to spreads and stops, and three ways to handle a release.
- [Forex Leverage Explained: Why 500:1 Is a Trap](https://gwhlds.com/hub/forex-leverage-explained.html): leverage as a margin requirement rather than buying power, the move that erases the deposit at each ratio, the ESMA 30:1 and CFTC 2%/5% caps, what offshore leverage costs you in protections, and why effective leverage comes from stop distance and position size.
- [Major, Minor and Exotic Pairs: Which to Actually Trade](https://gwhlds.com/hub/major-minor-and-exotic-pairs.html): the test that defines each of the three tiers, why the dollar sits on one side of 89.2% of global turnover, why a cross is really two trades on one ticket, and how the tier sets spread, swap, slippage and tradable hours.
- [How to Trade the London Open](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-to-trade-the-london-open.html): why London carries roughly 38% of global FX turnover, how to mark the Asian range before 08:00, the sweep that traps first-candle entries, two entries that survive it, and a two-hour session plan.
- [Futures Trading Guide: Contracts, Margin and Expiry](https://gwhlds.com/hub/futures-trading-guide.html): what a standardised futures contract actually obliges you to, why margin is a performance bond rather than a loan, the difference between exchange initial margin and broker day-trade margin, quarterly expiry and rollover, and why the pattern day trader rule does not reach futures.
- [E-mini vs Micro E-mini Futures: The Real Difference](https://gwhlds.com/hub/e-mini-and-micro-e-mini-futures.html): the one-tenth size rule, the contract multiplier behind MES, MNQ, MYM and M2K, what one contract really exposes an account to, the per-contract costs that do not shrink, and how to decide which size an account can support.
- [Tick Value Explained: How to Calculate Futures P&L](https://gwhlds.com/hub/futures-tick-value.html): tick size versus tick value versus point value, the multiplier formula that covers every contract, worked long trades on Micro Nasdaq and crude oil, and how to run the calculation backwards from a stop distance to a contract count.
- [Futures Margin Explained: Day vs Overnight Margin](https://gwhlds.com/hub/futures-margin-explained.html): why futures margin is a performance bond rather than a loan, how exchange initial and maintenance margin differ, why a broker's discounted day-trade margin expires at a daily cut-off, and how SPAN sets the levels.
- [How to Trade ES Futures: A Beginner's Guide](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-to-trade-es-futures.html): the E-mini S&P 500 contract in full — $50 per point, $12.50 per tick, quarterly expiry and third-Friday cash settlement — plus session timing, the honest ES-versus-MES comparison, and a first-trade sequence.
- [Futures Rollover: What It Is and When It Matters](https://gwhlds.com/hub/futures-contract-rollover.html): why every futures contract expires, how to read month codes, when liquidity migrates to the next contract, what the roll does to continuous charts and drawn levels, and the extra spot-month margin on deliverable contracts.
- [Why Futures Traders Watch the Cash Open](https://gwhlds.com/hub/futures-cash-open.html): why 9:30am ET matters when index futures already trade all night.
- [Trading Psychology: Why Discipline Beats Analysis](https://gwhlds.com/hub/trading-psychology.html): the four biases that cost traders most, and the rules that remove them.
- [Revenge Trading: Why It Happens and How to Stop](https://gwhlds.com/hub/revenge-trading.html): the break-even effect, the warning signs, and the rules that shut it down.
- [FOMO in Trading: How to Stop Chasing Candles](https://gwhlds.com/hub/fomo-in-trading.html): why a chased entry is arithmetically worse, what attention-driven buying costs, and the rules that prevent it.
- [How to Handle a Big Trading Loss Without Spiralling](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-to-handle-a-big-loss.html): a staged plan for the first hour, day and week after an outsized loss, and how to earn your size back.
- [Why You Cut Winners Early and Let Losers Run](https://gwhlds.com/hub/cutting-winners-early.html): the disposition effect measured across 10,000 brokerage accounts, and the exit rules that reverse it.
- [Analysis Paralysis in Trading: How to Break It](https://gwhlds.com/hub/analysis-paralysis-in-trading.html): the difference between analysis paralysis and fear, why stacked confirmations stop resolving, and how to cut a setup back to one rule.
- [Patience in Trading: Why Doing Nothing Is a Position](https://gwhlds.com/hub/patience-in-trading.html): why waiting is structurally cheap, how to design a session that assumes no trade, and how to score a no-trade day.
- [How Professional Traders Think About Being Wrong](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-traders-think-about-being-wrong.html): outcome bias measured across 692 participants, the four boxes a trade lands in, and why an unplanned winner is the costly one.
